rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers argue that the Prophet’s call cannot improve believers’ fortunes; they treat their own worldly comfort as proof that disbelief is true.
rows.anchor: وهو ردهم الدعوة النبوية بأنها لا تنفع في حسن حال المؤمنين بها شيئا ولو كانت حقة لجلبت إليهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām means dwelling, while nadī means an assembly, possibly specifically a council for consultation.
rows.anchor: المقام اسم مكان من القيام فهو المسكن، والندي هو المجلس وقيل خصوص مجلس المشاورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām can mark the audience of the message or its purpose of misleading believers; the address reading better fits the context.
rows.anchor: للتبليغ كما قيل، وقيل تفيد معنى التعليل أي قالوا لأجل الذين آمنوا أي لأجل إغوائهم وصرفهم عن الإيمان، والأول أنسب للسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in عليهم refers to people generally, believers and disbelievers, with قال الذين كفروا then replacing the pronoun explicitly.
rows.anchor: دون الكفار فقط حتى يكون قوله { قال الذين كفروا } من قبيل وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two groups are disbelievers and believers; disbelievers feign a question while asserting that their own dwellings and gatherings are superior.
rows.anchor: وكان مرادهم أن الكفار هم خير مقاما وأحسن نديا من المؤمنين الذين كان الغالب عليهم العبيد والفقراء لكنهم أوردوه في صورة السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarn denotes people living together in one period, and athāth denotes household furnishings.
rows.anchor: القرن الناس المقترنون في زمن واحد، والأثاث متاع البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some lexicographers say athāth is used only for a large quantity and has no singular form from the same root.
rows.anchor: قيل لا يطلق إلا على الكثير ولا واحد له من لفظه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ says raʾy here means visible appearance, not the verbal noun; raʾy is the act of seeing and raʾy is what is seen.
rows.anchor: نقل في مجمع البيان عن بعضهم أنه اسم لما ظهر وليس بالمصدر وإنما المصدر الرأي والرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers overlook human life after death, which is everlasting; a few worldly days count for little against eternity and cannot secure happiness.
rows.anchor: أن للإنسان حياة خالدة أبدية لا منتهى لها وإنما سعادته في سعادتها والأيام القلائل التي يعيش فيها في الدنيا لا قدر لها قبال ما لا نهاية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly pleasures neither guarantee happiness nor protect people from divine anger; a life threatened by destruction is no secure blessing.
rows.anchor: هذه التمتعات الدنيوية لا تحتم له السعادة ولا تقيه من غضب الله إن حل به يوما وما هو من الظالمين ببعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is circumstantial and كم is an exclamatory report, not a question: many earlier peoples had better furnishings and appearances yet were destroyed.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الجملة حالية وكم خبرية لا استفهامية، والمعنى أنهم يتفوهون بهذه الشبهة الواهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boast recalls Pharaoh, who cited his Egyptian kingdom and rivers to claim superiority, then was drowned and made an example for later peoples.
rows.anchor: وقد نقل سبحانه نظير هذه الشبهة عن فرعون وعقبه بحديث غرقه وهلاكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb kāna indicates that the people persist in misguidance, not merely that they fell into it once.
rows.anchor: تدل على استمرارهم في الضلالة لا مجرد تحقق ضلالة ما، وبذلك يتم التهديد بمجازاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-person imperative falyamdud means that God obliges Himself to extend the period of misguidance, since a speaker ordering another to command something undertakes it Himself.
rows.anchor: صيغة أمر غائب ويؤل معناه إلى أن من الواجب على الرحمن أن يمده مدا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says imdād is more commonly used for favorable things, while madd is more commonly used for harmful things; both mean extension here.
rows.anchor: ذكر الراغب في المفردات أن أكثر ما جاء الإمداد في المحبوب والمد في المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God extends worldly adornments to those settled in misguidance, drawing them further from truth; they recognize the truth only when punishment or the Hour arrives too late.
rows.anchor: فقد أوجب الله على نفسه أن يمده بما منه ضلالته كالزخارف الدنيوية في مورد الكلام فينصرف بذلك عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extension is abandonment disguised as favor: worldly distractions defer recognition of truth until punishment or resurrection, when recognition cannot help.
rows.anchor: هذا المد خذلان في صورة إكرام والمراد به أن ينصرف عن الحق واتباعه بالاشتغال بزهرة الحياة الدنيا الغارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief has no benefit once punishment is seen or a decisive sign arrives, as stated in the linked verses of Ghāfir and al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا سنة الله التي قد خلت في عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun in رأوا follows the meaning of من, while the singular له in فليمدد follows its grammatical form.
rows.anchor: رعاية جانب معناه كما أن في إرجاع ضمير الأفراد في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the worse place and weaker forces answers the disbelievers’ earlier comparison of the two groups.
rows.anchor: قوبل به قولهم السابق { أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the worldly punishment, the disbelievers’ place is wherever God’s punishment overtakes them; for Quraysh leaders it was the well of Badr where their bodies were thrown.
rows.anchor: أما مكانهم حين يرون العذاب - والظاهر أن المراد به عذاب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Hour their place is eternal Hell, and their forces are weak because nothing protects them from God and their prepared resources prove useless.
rows.anchor: وأما مكانهم يوم يرون الساعة فالنار الخالدة التي هي دار البوار، وأما ضعف جندهم فلأنه لا عاصم لهم اليوم من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abiding good works are righteous deeds preserved with God, followed by gracious thanks and immense reward.
rows.anchor: الباقيات الصالحات الأعمال الصالحة التي تبقى محفوظة عند الله وتستعقب جميل الشكر وعظيم الأجر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains thawāb as a return to an original or intended state, hence the recompense returned to a person for their deeds; it is used for good or evil but usually for good.
rows.anchor: قال في المفردات أصل الثوب رجوع الشيء إلى حالته الأولى التي كان عليها أو إلى الحالة المقدرة المقصودة بالفكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mard is a place noun from returning and means Paradise.
rows.anchor: والمرد اسم مكان من الرد والمراد به الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses give a second answer to the worldly boast: God further guides believers to lasting good works and a permanent home, better than the disbelievers’ fleeting luxuries; عند ربك marks this as an infallible divine judgment.
rows.anchor: جواب ثان عن حجة الكفار أعني قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next four verses portray someone who heard the disbelievers, was swayed to join them, and claimed that adopting their polytheism would bring wealth and children.
rows.anchor: أن بعض الناس ممن آمن بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أو كان في معرض ذلك بعدما سمع قول الكفار مال إليهم ولحق بهم قائلا لأوتين مالا وولدا

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most commentators, following reports about the occasion of revelation, identify the speaker as a Quraysh polytheist who said this to Khabbāb when asked to repay a debt, claiming he would receive wealth and children in Paradise.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره الأكثر بالبناء على ما ورد من سبب النزول أن الجملة قول أحد المتعرقين في الشرك من قريش خاطب به خباب بن الأرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that setting: Quraysh polytheists did not affirm resurrection, so a promise of post-resurrection wealth would be mockery, which the following argument cannot answer.
rows.anchor: ما كانوا مذعنين بالبعث أصلا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم المفسر
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says the verse applies generally to anyone with this trait; the author also judges this reading inadequate to the passage’s context.
rows.anchor: ما نقل عن أبي مسلم المفسر أن الآية عامة فيمن له هذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is an exclamation linked by فاء to the prior boast: this person’s disbelief and promise share the same belief that paganism brings worldly success.
rows.anchor: مسوق للتعجيب، وكلمة { أفرأيت } كلمة تعجيب وقد فرعه بفاء التفريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath lām and emphatic nūn show that the speaker swears he will receive wealth and children, treating disbelief as a blessed path to power and happiness.
rows.anchor: وقد أقسم بذلك كما يشهد به لام القسم ونون التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two rhetorical questions deny that the speaker knows the unseen or has a covenant with God; he has no basis for certainty that disbelief will bring the promised reward.
rows.anchor: فليس بمطلع على الغيب حتى يعلم بأنه سيؤتى بكفره ما يأمله ولا بمتخذ عهدا عند الله حتى يطمئن إليه في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā is a rebuke: disbelief does not cause wealth and children; the actual consequence of his claim and disbelief is extended punishment.
rows.anchor: كلا كلمة ردع وزجر وذيل الآية دليل على أنه سبحانه يرد بها ما يتضمنه قول هذا القائل من ترتب إيتاء المال والولد على الكفر بآيات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the author’s preferred reading, the man dies and leaves behind his claim that disbelief would give him wealth and children; it remains attached to him as a sin preserved by God.
rows.anchor: أنه سيموت ويفنى ويترك قوله لأوتين بكفري مالا وولدا، وقد كان خطيئة لازمة له لزوم المال للإنسان محفوظة عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He comes to God alone, without anything he relied on or used for support, carrying only the statement preserved against him and facing its consequence.
rows.anchor: أي وحده وليس معه شيء مما كان ينتصر به ويركن إليه بحسب وهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearest reading of writing his words is establishing them so their consequence follows, rather than recording them in a ledger; the next verse would otherwise repeat the point without an evident purpose.
rows.anchor: تثبيته ليترتب عليه أثره لا كتابته في صحيفة عمله

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: On the majority reading, the speaker is ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who swears he will receive wealth and children in Paradise after resurrection; God asks whether he knows the unseen or has a covenant, then strips him of possessions and brings him alone.
rows.anchor: بناء على كونه ناظرا إلى الإيتاء في الآخرة كما اختاره الأكثر فمعنى الآيات كما فسروها تعجب من الذي كفر بآياتنا وهو عاص بن وائل أو وليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report in Tafsīr al-Qummī identifies the man as ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil; when Khabbāb sought his debt, he promised to pay it with better wealth in Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbāb reports that ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil refused to repay his debt unless Khabbāb disbelieved in Muḥammad; Khabbāb refused even if ʿĀṣ died and was raised.
rows.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال كنت رجلا قينا وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين فأتيته أتقاضاه

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: The report continues that ʿĀṣ said he would return after death with wealth and children to repay Khabbāb; the author notes similar accounts from al-Ṭabarānī, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr via al-Ḥasan and an unnamed Companion, and Ibn ʿAbbās via Companions, without grading them.
rows.anchor: قال فإني إذا مت ثم بعثت جئتني ولي ثم مال وولد فاعطيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports do not fit the context: they make the saying a mockery by someone who denied resurrection, whereas the passage answers it with a serious argument.
rows.anchor: على صراحتها في كونها كلمة استهزاء لا تنطبق على الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the statement were a taunt meant to corner Khabbāb rather than a sincere claim, mentioning children lacks a rationale because early Muslims were not known to teach procreation in Paradise.
rows.anchor: لم يكن لذكر الولد مع المال وجه وكفاه أن يقول لأوتين مالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic oath, unqualified promise of being given wealth, and question about unseen knowledge or covenant are inexplicable as mere dialectical cornering.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن للقسم والتأكيد البالغ في قوله { لأوتين } وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An argument from unseen knowledge is irrelevant to a mere taunt, since such a taunt need not depend on the speaker believing the premise he uses against an opponent.
rows.anchor: إذ الإلزام والتبكيت لا يتوقف على العلم بصدق ما يلزم به حتى يتوقف عن منشأ علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from the Prophet and the Imams about the abiding good works were discussed earlier under the commentary on al-Kahf 18:46.
rows.anchor: أخبار عن النبي وأئمة أهل البيت عليهم أفضل الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the third part of the disbelievers’ claims: they associate partners with God and say that the Merciful has taken a child.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الفصل الثالث مما نقل عنهم وهو شركهم بالله باتخاذ الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their alleged gods include angels, jinn, holy human figures, and powerful kings, since many treated kingship as a heavenly sanctity.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الآلهة هم الملائكة والجن والقديسون من الإنس وجبابرة الملوك فإن أكثرهم كانوا يرون الملك قداسة سماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They regard the gods as intercessors who bring worldly benefits and protection, thereby granting honor; interpreting the verse as afterlife intercession misses that polytheists denied resurrection.
rows.anchor: كونهم لهم عزا كونهم شفعاء لهم يقربونهم إلى الله بالشفاعة فينالون بذلك العزة في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that their hoped-for honor is intercession in the afterlife is rejected because the polytheists did not believe in resurrection.
rows.anchor: ومن فسر كونهم لهم عزا بشفاعتهم لهم في الآخرة خفي عليه أن المشركين لا يقولون بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍidd means an incompatible opposite; al-Akhfash allows it to denote either one or many, while others object, and the singular here treats the united hostile gods as one.
rows.anchor: الضد بحسب اللغة المنافي الذي لا يجتمع مع الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns most naturally make the gods reject the polytheists’ worship and become their enemies; this is illustrated by al-Naḥl and Fāṭir.
rows.anchor: والمعنى سيكفر الآلهة بعبادة هؤلاء المشركين ويكون الآلهة حال كونهم على المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reverses the pronouns: polytheists repudiate their worship of gods and become the gods’ enemies, as in al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: أن التعبير المناسب لهذا المعنى أن يقال سيكفرون بهم على حد ما يقال كفر بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative is unlikely: ḍidd is set against ʿizz and thus describes the gods; the pronoun pattern points to gods as the deniers, and idiom would say they deny the gods rather than their worship.
rows.anchor: نظرا إلى خصوص ترتب الضمائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression should be that the gods disbelieve in the polytheists’ worship, not that they disbelieve in the gods themselves; this supports the preferred pronoun reading.
rows.anchor: سيكفرون بهم على حد ما يقال كفر بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gods’ rejection and hostility are the reality disclosed on Judgment Day, not a new change arising then; otherwise the verse’s proof would fail.
rows.anchor: هو ظهور حقيقة الأمر يومئذ فإن شأن يوم القيامة ظهور الحقائق فيه لأهل الجمع لا حدوثها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azz and hazz both mean forceful agitation: Satanic forces stir the disbelievers toward evil, corruption, falsehood, and deviation from steadfast truth.
rows.anchor: الأز والهز بمعنى واحد وهو التحريك بشدة وإزعاج والمراد تهييج الشياطين إياهم إلى الشر والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sending the devils is retributive: disbelief is answered with increased misguidance; the phrase على الكافرين supports this, whereas ابتداءً would use a pronoun.
rows.anchor: ولا ضير في نسبة إرسال الشياطين إليه تعالى بعد ما كان على طريق المجازاة فإنهم كفروا بالحق فجازاهم الله بزيادة الكفر والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Introduced as evidence, this verse supports the claim that false gods oppose their worshippers: the jinn devils among those gods drive them toward ruin under God’s permission.
rows.anchor: المفيد معنى الاستشهاد مسوقة لتأييد ما ذكر في الآية السابقة من كون آلهتهم عليهم ضدا

rows.speaker: صاحب روح المعاني
rows.claim: The author of Rūḥ al-Maʿānī connects this verse to the sequence beginning with the human question about resurrection and ending with the gods opposing their worshippers.
rows.anchor: وجعل صاحب روح المعاني هذه الآية مترتبة على مجموع الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that long connection as unhelpful because it disrupts the passage’s flow and the relation of the following verses to this one.
rows.anchor: وأطنب في بيان كيفية الاتصال بما لا يجدي نفعا وأفسد بذلك سياق الآيات واتصال ما بعد هذه الآية بما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counting depicts the consumption of their lifetimes: breaths are stored in a count and sent one by one until their appointed end arrives.
rows.anchor: والعد يفني المعدود وينفده وبهذه العناية قصد به إنفاد أعمارهم والانتهاء إلى آخر أنفاسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life on earth is a period of testing and forming the person’s enduring self, as indicated by al-Kahf 18:7.
rows.anchor: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The count in truth tallies deeds entered into the record of a lifetime, building what a person will experience in the afterlife; the surface may suggest breaths or days.
rows.anchor: كان العد بالحقيقة عدا للأعمال المثبتة في صحيفة العمر، ليتم بذلك بنية الحياة الأخروية الخالدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a fetus’s time in the womb completes its body, a person’s time in the world completes the soul and its allotted recompense.
rows.anchor: فكما أن مكث الجنين في الرحم مدة يتم به خلقة جسمه كذلك مكث الإنسان في الدنيا لأن يتم به خلقة نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no reason to hasten death for either a wicked disbeliever, whose misdeeds are being counted, or a righteous believer, whose good deeds are being counted for reward.
rows.anchor: فلا ينبغي للإنسان أن يستعجل الموت لكافر طالح لأن مدة بقائه مدة عد سيئاته ليحاسب عليها ويعذب بها ولا لمؤمن صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to hurry follows from the previous discussion, while God’s counting explains the delay: all remain under His power, so the Prophet should not be distressed by postponed judgment.
rows.anchor: وهو في الحقيقة علة التأخير ومحصل المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafd are people arriving to visit or seek a need; they are called a delegation only when riding, and the plural has singular wāfid.
rows.anchor: الوفد هم القوم الواردون لزيارة أو استنجاز حاجة أو نحو ذلك ولا يسمون وفدا إلا إذا كانوا ركبانا وهو جمع واحده وافد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between going to the Merciful and being driven to Hell may imply that the pious are gathered to Paradise, the place of nearness to God.
rows.anchor: قوله في الآية التالية { إلى جهنم } أن المراد بحشرهم إلى الرحمن حشرهم إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wird means thirsty people, by association with approaching water to drink; thirst is implied in such an approach.
rows.anchor: فسر الورد بالعطاش وكأنه مأخوذ من ورود الماء أي قصده ليشرب ولا يكون ذلك إلا عن عطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the gathered groups pious and criminals signals the cause of their respective destinations: piety for nearness to God and criminality for the drive to Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي تعليق السوق إلى جهنم بوصف الإجرام إشعار بالعلية ونظيره تعليق الحشر إلى الرحمن في الآية السابقة بوصف التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a second answer to the claim that idols intercede: only select beings admitted by God’s covenant possess intercession, not every being people choose as a god.
rows.anchor: وهذا جواب ثان عن اتخاذهم الآلهة للشفاعة وهو أن ليس كل من يهوى الإنسان شفاعته فاتخذه إلها ليشفع له يكون شفيعا بل إنما يملك الشفاعة بعهد من الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the covenant belong to those receiving intercession: belief in God and affirmation of prophecy.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد إن المشفع لهم لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا والعهد هو الإيمان بالله والتصديق بالنبوة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is God’s promise of intercession to prophets, Imams, believers, and angels, as stated in reports.
rows.anchor: وقيل وعده تعالى له بالشفاعة كما في الأنبياء والأئمة والمؤمنين والملائكة على ما في الأخبار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation is the testimony that none is god but God, disavowing self-reliance, and hoping only in God.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن يتبرأ من الحول والقوة وأن لا يرجو إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation, that only God’s chosen possess the right to intercede, best fits the context.
rows.anchor: والوجه الأول هو الأوجه وهو بالسياق أنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the Merciful took a child is attributed to idolaters and some of their adherents; some present it as honor, while others teach actual derivation from divine essence, which the verse means and the following argument refutes.
rows.anchor: قال بذلك تحقيقا بمعنى الاشتقاق من حقيقة اللاهوت واشتمال الولد على جوهرة والده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idd means a terrible and repugnant matter; the near-splitting heavens, splitting earth, and collapsing mountains make the gravity of claiming a child tangible.
rows.anchor: الإد بكسر الهمزة الشيء المنكر الفظيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every being’s coming as God’s servant means appearing before Him in complete ownership: no creature independently owns benefit, harm, death, life, or resurrection, and this servitude holds throughout existence.
rows.anchor: المراد بإتيان كل منهم عبدا له توجه الكل إليه ومثوله بين يديه في صفة المملوكية المحضة فكل منهم مملوك له لا يملك لنفسه نفعا ولا ضرا ولا موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the verse about coming alone at Judgment, this verse does not specify Judgment Day because the state of servitude is already actual and continuous.
rows.anchor: ولذا لم يقيد الإتيان في الآية بالقيامة بخلاف ما في الآية الرابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s counting and enumeration establish each creature’s servitude, position, provisions, and assigned functions, as though entered in a register of servants.
rows.anchor: والمراد بإحصائهم وعدهم تثبيت العبودية لهم فإن العبيد إنما تتعين لهم أرزاقهم وتتبين وظائفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Judgment each comes empty-handed; apparent worldly power, wealth, children, allies, and means are revealed never to have been truly owned.
rows.anchor: إتيانه يومئذ صفر الكف لا يملك شيئا مما كان يملكه بحسب ظاهر النظر في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage offers one argument against divine offspring: every being is wholly owned, counted, assigned a role, and finally appears alone; such need and poverty cannot coexist with divinity or derivation from God’s essence.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان هذا حال كل من في السماوات والأرض فكيف يمكن أن يكون بعضهم ولدا لله واجدا لحقيقة اللاهوت مشتقا من جوهرتها، وكيف تجتمع الألوهية والفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers in a creator, whether monotheists or polytheists, agree that all existence ends with one creator; they differ over multiple objects of worship and delegated lords or managers.
rows.anchor: فمما لا يرتاب فيه مثبتو الصانع سواء في ذلك الموحدون والمشركون وإنما الاختلاف في كثرة المعبود ووحدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises to place love for believers who do good in hearts, without specifying whose hearts, whether in this life or the next, or restricting it to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعد جميل منه تعالى أنه سيجعل للذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات مودة في القلوب ولم يقيده بما بينهم أنفسهم ولا بغيرهم ولا بدنيا ولا بآخرة أو جنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah closes by describing the Quran’s descent from its inaccessible reality into the Prophet’s speech, so he can give glad tidings to the pious, warn stubborn opponents, and recall earlier peoples’ destruction.
rows.anchor: الآيتان ختام السورة يذكر سبحانه فيهما تنزيل حقيقة القرآن وهي أعلى من أن تنالها أيدى الأفهام العادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Facilitation implies an earlier state in which the Quran was not readily recited or understood; al-Zukhruf describes it as lofty and resistant to ordinary understanding before it was made Arabic.
rows.anchor: التيسير وهو التسهيل ينبئ عن حال سابقة ما كان يسهل معها تلاوته ولا فهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred sense of making it easy in the Prophet’s tongue is rendering it in Arabic, which makes warning and glad tidings possible and better fits the earlier verses and surah context.
rows.anchor: فتنبئ الآية أنه تعالى يسره بلسانه ليتيسر له التبشير والإنذار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says God made the Quran flow on the Prophet’s tongue through revelation and singled him out to receive divine speech; the author considers it profound but less fitting to context.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن معنى تيسيره بلسانه إجراؤه على لسانه بالوحي واختصاصه بوحي الكلام الإلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ludd are the Prophet’s people, and the word is the plural of aladd, meaning a fierce disputant.
rows.anchor: المراد قومه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، واللد جمع ألد من اللدد وهو الخصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥsās means sensory perception and rakz means sound, with perception given as its original sense; previous generations vanished so completely that no person or voice remains to be sensed.
rows.anchor: الإحساس هو الإدراك بالحس، والركز هو الصوت، قيل والأصل في معناه الحس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning reassures that these argumentative people cannot frustrate God: He destroyed many earlier generations, and none of them can now be perceived or heard.
rows.anchor: فكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن فبادوا فلا يحس منهم أحد ولا يسمع لهم صوت
